name: Mastercard

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Runs the Mastercard card network (routes and settles payments between banks, merchants and cardholders) and sells fraud, data, cyber and other services on top. 3.8B cards issued; GDV $3.0T in Q3 2026.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Q3 2026 net revenue $9.81B: payment network $5.75B (59%), value-added services and solutions $4.06B (41%, +19% y/y). Network gross assessments: domestic $3.2B, cross-border $3.8B, transaction processing $4.8B.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Customers are issuing banks and acquirers, not consumers; rebates and incentives to them were $6.37B in Q3, 53% of gross network revenue (39% of gross revenue incl. services), up 18% y/y. Large issuers hold bargaining power; each deal renewal can reset economics. Customer concentration table not re-read in this pass.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: Global: worldwide-less-US GDV +8% vs US +6% in Q3. Functional currencies USD, EUR, GBP, BRL; YTD net revenue +15% reported vs +13% currency-neutral, so FX has been a tailwind that a stronger dollar (+4.8% 3m) reverses.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Fees on volume, cross-border volume and transactions switched, plus service subscriptions; asset-light, no credit risk on cards. Rebates netted from revenue. Q3 operating margin 59.8% GAAP (60.5% adjusted).

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Mostly fixed cost base: net revenue +14% vs adjusted opex +12% in Q3, margin up 0.7pt. Capex plus capitalised software 9M 2026 $1.14B vs $0.93B (about 4% of revenue). Prepaid expenses (customer incentive payments) rose $4.7B in 9M. Guidance hit rate not tested.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Few physical inputs: own data centres/cloud, engineering and security labour, and bank/settlement partners; no single-supplier chokepoint found in this pass. Industry tags: regulation, consumer_spending_nominal, inflation, dollar, wages. Cost pass-through: network fees are priced on volume, so inflation lifts nominal volume (inflation passes through automatically) while labour cost is not passed on (adjusted opex +12%). Dollar tag: cross-border revenue is measured in constant dollars, so a stronger dollar shrinks translated revenue. The real exposure is the customer side: rebates rising faster than revenue (+18%).

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Two-network duopoly with Visa, 3.8B cards, switching costs for banks, scale. Doing differently now: services (fraud, data, cyber) now 41% of Q3 net revenue, agentic commerce, and the BVNK stablecoin infrastructure buy (net assets acquired $1.56B on 2026-08-03).

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Brand on 3.8B cards; used on every swipe; consumers would notice if it vanished. Pricing power shown: 'pricing' is cited as a driver of both network and services growth in Q3.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Visa is the main rival (Jul-Sep payments volume +9%, cross-border +14%); Mastercard Q3 GDV +7%, cross-border +11%, so it is growing a little slower than Visa on volume but faster on services. Also AmEx, Discover and real-time bank-to-bank rails. Share trend vs Visa roughly flat to slightly down on volume.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Services +19% (+20% YTD) and growing as a share; cross-border +11% local; switched transactions +9%; cash-to-card and B2B still open. Runway is well known and priced (see read 17).

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: FY2025 operating cash flow $17.6B; est. FCF about $16.4B after capex ($489M) and capitalised software; LTM FCF about $15.4B (est.). 9M 2026 buybacks $11.9B at average $520.64 plus dividends: roughly 100%+ of FCF returned. Debt $23.9B vs cash $10.1B. Insiders each under 1%. Pay scored on adjusted EPS, net revenue (2025 bonus 145% of target). 9M OCF fell 6% on incentive prepayments and litigation settlement cash.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Gaining relevance (more electronic spend, services added). Risks: regulation, interchange litigation, bank-to-bank/real-time and stablecoin rails, issuer concentration. CEO Miebach in place; CFO rotated Aug 2026 in an orderly handover.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 8-K Item 4.01 or 4.02, no NT filings, no CORRESP/UPLOAD comment letters since Feb 2023 (outside 3 years). 5.02 items in 2026 are orderly CFO/controller rotations. Litigation: Block and Intuit opt-out claims seek over $5B single damages; accrued litigation fell to $262M from $800M. Adjusted vs GAAP gap small (EPS $5.31 vs $5.28).

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat 0/+ (nominal volume inflated, float; but dollar +4.8% hurts translation and cross-border); Slowdown 0 (cross-border and travel soften first, but networks fall least); Stagflation 0; Boom +. Q3 GDV +7% local vs +9% purchase volume. Real spend flat in October: nominal volume growth is partly price. Rates: no credit book, mild debt cost.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Live exposure: interchange class actions (Second Circuit appeal on damages class release, Sept 2026), Block/Intuit opt-outs, Credit Card Competition Act, Durbin cap vacated by Eighth Circuit (Oct 26, from brief; not found in the 10-Q text). Cap lift or routing mandates would shift who keeps the spread. Cuts both ways: a vacated debit cap helps issuers, not the network directly.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $659.97, EV about $588B. Reverse DCF at 10% discount, 3% terminal, LTM FCF about $15.4B needs about 16% FCF growth for 10 years; own FCF growth 2021-25 about 17-18% a year (2020 base is Covid-low). Trailing P/E 34.5 and forward 28.5 vs MA year-end range 33-40 (2021-25); Visa 34.4/24.8, AmEx 17.6, PayPal 11.0. FCF yield about 2.7%. Price sits near 52-week high ($681.99). Services stream is priced in.

status_reason: Excellent business, but today's price needs about 16% FCF growth for 10 years, matching its best run, so there is no cushion and no mispricing.

feedback.note: Mastercard Q3: cross-border +11% local (10% USD), GDV +7%, services +19%, no sign yet of a spending slowdown in card data; Visa Jul-Sep payments volume +9%, cross-border +14%. Hard data confirm Overheat for card volume; the real-spend weakness is not visible in network volume yet.
